exercise.name: Plank Jack

reference.title: Plank Jack
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips; Waist, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (dynamic plank: anti-extension hold with hip abduction hops)

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily and rhythmically; do not hold the breath.
breathing.cadence: About one jack (out and in) per second

prescription.tempo: Quick, light hops at about one jack per second
prescription.progression: Longer sets, then faster jacks, then plank jacks with a push-up

cues.text: High plank: hands under the shoulders, arms straight, body in one line, feet together on the balls of the feet.
Hop both feet out to about twice hip width; land softly on the balls of the feet.
Hop them back together. Hips stay level: no piking up or sagging.
Keep a steady rhythm; hands and shoulders stay still, abs braced.
Finish in the plank with the feet together.

mistakes.fix: Brace harder, slow down and make the hops smaller.
Squeeze the glutes and pull the ribs down; drop to the knees between sets if needed.
Keep the shoulders over the wrists.
Land lightly on the balls of the feet.

kinematics.norm: Shoulders, hips and ankles in one line; hips stay level as the feet move (clinical opinion)
Feet hop from together to about twice hip width (clinical opinion)
Hands under the shoulders, elbows straight, planted (clinical opinion)
On the balls of the feet, short low hops (clinical opinion)
About one jack per second (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Escamilla, Lewis, Pecson, Imamura and Andrews 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379; PMC4922527)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wrist pain: plank on the fists or on dumbbell handles, or do step-out plank jacks.
Shoulder pain or recent shoulder injury: get guidance before weight-bearing on the hands.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before plank and jumping work.
modify: Step the feet out and in one at a time (no hop).
Hands on a bench (incline plank jack).
regressions: Alternating side steps in a plank.
progressions: Plank jack with a push-up every few jacks.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis holds the trunk against sagging: a plank on the toes is about 34% upper and 40% lower rectus MVIC (Escamilla 2016). The hops add brief impacts the trunk must absorb without the hips dipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: External and internal obliques were about 40% and 29% MVIC in a plank on the toes (Escamilla 2016); they also resist the side-to-side shift as the feet move.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: External and internal obliques were about 40% and 29% MVIC in a plank on the toes (Escamilla 2016); they also resist the side-to-side shift as the feet move.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Abducts the legs to jump the feet out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Abducts the legs to jump the feet out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Bring the feet back in (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Bring the feet back in (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the rib cage while the hands bear weight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the rib cage while the hands bear weight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Supports the body over the hands (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Supports the body over the hands (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Supports the body over the hands (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Supports the body over the hands (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight in the plank (rectus femoris about 20% MVIC in a plank on the toes, Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight in the plank (rectus femoris about 20% MVIC in a plank on the toes, Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off and land on the balls of the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off and land on the balls of the feet (clinical opinion).
